# Item Layouts

Headers: `winui/ui/layouts/Layout.hpp`, `winui/ui/layouts/StackLayout.hpp`, `winui/ui/layouts/TileLayout.hpp`, `winui/ui/layouts/WrapLayout.hpp`, `winui/ui/layouts/LinedFlowLayout.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/layouts/StackLayout.hpp`.

The base of every attachable layout. Not copyable: it belongs to one host.

Derive from [NonVirtualizingLayout](#class-nonvirtualizinglayout) or [VirtualizingLayout](#class-virtualizinglayout), not from this class. A host takes the layout by `std::unique_ptr` ([LayoutPanelControl::set_layout()](../layout/layout-panel.md#set_layout), [ForEachControl::set_layout()](for-each.md#set_layout)) and becomes its [owner()](#owner). The layout keeps its per-host state in its own members and calls [invalidate_measure()](#invalidate_measure) when one of its properties changes.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  panel  = std::make_unique<ui::LayoutPanelControl>();
auto* layout = panel->set_layout(std::make_unique<ui::StackLayoutEngine>());
layout->set_spacing(8.0f); // the layout invalidates the panel
```

## `ui::StackLayout`

Items one after another in a line, like the children of a [ui::VerticalStack](../layout/stack.md#uiverticalstack) or [ui::HorizontalStack](../layout/stack.md#uihorizontalstack). Builds a [ui::StackLayoutEngine](#class-stacklayoutengine).

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::ForEach<std::string>{
    .items  = {"One", "Two", "Three"},
    .layout = ui::StackLayout{.orientation = ui::Orientation::Horizontal, .spacing = 8.0f},
    .item   = [](const std::string& text) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Text{.text = text}; },
});
```

```cpp
    .orientation, .spacing
}
```

| <span id="uistacklayout-spacing"></span>`spacing` | `float` | `0.0f` | Gap between adjacent items, DIPs. |

## `ui::WrapLayout`

Items at their own size in a line that wraps, like the children of a [ui::WrapPanel](../layout/wrap-panel.md#uiwrappanel). Builds a [ui::WrapLayoutEngine](#class-wraplayoutengine).

Example:

```cpp
window.set_content(ui::ForEach<std::string>{
    .items  = {"news", "sport", "travel"},
    .layout = ui::WrapLayout{.min_item_spacing = 8.0f, .line_spacing = 8.0f},
    .item   = [](const std::string& tag) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Button{.text = tag}; },
});
```

## `ui::TileLayout`

## class NonVirtualizingLayout

Derives from `ui::Layout`.

A layout that measures and arranges every child of the host.

Derive a custom layout for a fixed set of children from it and give it to a [LayoutPanel](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel). Each pass sees all children through the context. Keep any state between [measure()](#measure) and [arrange()](#arrange) in members.

Example: 
```cpp
// Every child in one column, each as tall as it wants.
class ColumnLayout final : public ui::NonVirtualizingLayout
{
public:
    ui::Size measure(ui::NonVirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size available) override
    {
        ui::Size total{};
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < context.item_count(); ++i)
        {
            const ui::Size d = context.measure(i, {available.width, ui::Unbounded});
            total.width = std::max(total.width, d.width);
            total.height += d.height;
        }
        return total;
    }
    ui::Size arrange(ui::NonVirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size final_size) override
    {
        float y = 0.0f;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < context.item_count(); ++i)
        {
            const float h = context.desired_size(i).height;
            context.arrange(i, ui::Rect{0.0f, y, final_size.width, h});
            y += h;
        }
        return final_size;
    }
};

window.set_content(ui::LayoutPanel{
    .layout   = std::make_unique<ColumnLayout>(),
    .content  = {ui::Text{.text = "One"}, ui::Text{.text = "Two"}},
});
```

### measure

```cpp
virtual Size measure(NonVirtualizingLayoutContext& context, Size available) = 0
```

Returns the size the children need within `available` (infinity on an unbounded axis). It must measure every child it will arrange.

### arrange

```cpp
virtual Size arrange(NonVirtualizingLayoutContext& context, Size final_size) = 0
```

Places every child within `final_size` and returns the size used.

## class VirtualizingLayout

Derives from `ui::Layout`.

A layout that measures and arranges the part of a collection that is in view.

Derive a custom layout from it and give it to a [ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach), which can then virtualize, or to a [LayoutPanel](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel), where every child is in view. [measure()](#measure) realizes only the items inside [VirtualizingLayoutContext::realization_rect()](#realization_rect) and returns the extent of the whole collection. [arrange()](#arrange) places the items [measure()](#measure) realized.

Example: 
```cpp
// Fixed-height rows; only the rows in the realization rect are realized.
class RowLayout final : public ui::VirtualizingLayout
{
public:
    ui::Size measure(ui::VirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size available) override
    {
        const ui::Rect view  = context.realization_rect();
        const std::size_t count = context.item_count();
        first_ = std::min(count, static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(0.0f, view.y) / Row));
        last_  = std::min(count, static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(0.0f, view.bottom()) / Row) + 1);
        for (std::size_t i = first_; i < last_; ++i)
        {
            (void)context.measure(context.get_or_create_element_at(i), {available.width, Row});
        }
        return {std::isfinite(available.width) ? available.width : 0.0f, static_cast<float>(count) * Row};
    }
    ui::Size arrange(ui::VirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size final_size) override
    {
        for (std::size_t i = first_; i < last_; ++i)
        {
            context.arrange(context.get_or_create_element_at(i),
                            ui::Rect{0.0f, static_cast<float>(i) * Row, final_size.width, Row});
        }
        return final_size;
    }

private:
    static constexpr float Row = 32.0f;
    std::size_t            first_ = 0;
    std::size_t            last_  = 0;
};

auto repeater = std::make_unique<ui::ForEachControl>();
repeater->set_layout(std::make_unique<RowLayout>());
```

## class StackLayoutEngine

Derives from `ui::VirtualizingLayout`.

A virtualizing layout that places items one after another, [`spacing`](#spacing) apart. A [ui::ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach) or a [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) stacks its items with it.

Only the items in or near the viewport are realized. The rest are estimated at the average measured size, so the scroll extent stays stable. Every item gets the full cross extent. It also works in a [LayoutPanel](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel), where every child is realized.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> rows = {"Inbox", "Drafts", "Sent"}; // outlives the window

auto  scroll   = std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>();
auto* repeater = scroll->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::ForEachControl>());
auto* stack    = repeater->set_layout(std::make_unique<ui::StackLayoutEngine>());
stack->set_orientation(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
stack->set_spacing(8.0f);
repeater->set_item_template([&rows](std::size_t i) { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(rows[i]); });
repeater->set_item_count(rows.size());
window.set_content(std::move(scroll));
```

## class TileLayoutEngine

Derives from `ui::VirtualizingLayout`.

A virtualizing layout that puts every item in an equal-sized cell, as many cells per line as fit, line after line.

The cell is exactly [min_item_width()](#min_item_width) x [min_item_height()](#min_item_height) where those are set, else item 0's desired size. Hand it to a [ui::ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach) or a [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) through set_layout() or the spec's `.layout`. Only the lines inside the realization window are realized, but the extent covers every line, so a scroller can jump anywhere. Every setter lays out the host again.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> names = {"Ada", "Grace", "Linus", "Margaret"};

auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::TileLayoutEngine>();
grid->set_min_item_width(120.0f);
grid->set_min_item_height(80.0f);
grid->set_min_row_spacing(8.0f);
grid->set_min_column_spacing(8.0f);
grid->set_items_stretch(ui::TileLayoutItemsStretch::Fill);

window.set_content(ui::Scroll{
    .height  = 400.0f,
    .content = ui::ForEach<std::string>{
        .items      = names,
        .layout     = std::move(grid),
        .virtualize = true,
        .item       = [](const std::string& name) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Text{.text = name}; },
    },
});
```

### set_group_sizes

```cpp
void set_group_sizes(std::vector<std::size_t> sizes)
```

Lays the indices out in groups: each group is one index for its header, which takes a line of its own across the whole width, then `sizes[g]` indices in cells, from the start of a new line. The indices run header, its items, the next header, and so on. Every header is as tall as the first one, the cells are sized from the first item, and a line's cells start at its leading edge. An empty vector (the default) lays every index out as a cell. Lays out the host again. A grouped [ui::TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) sets it.

## class WrapLayoutEngine

Derives from `ui::VirtualizingLayout`.

A virtualizing [ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach) layout that places items of any size one after another and wraps to a new line when the next one would not fit. Only the items that show are realized.

Every item keeps its own desired size. Items sit [min_item_spacing()](#min_item_spacing) apart along a line. Lines are as thick as their largest item and [line_spacing()](#line_spacing) apart, and [line_alignment()](#line_alignment) spreads the items of each line. Lines outside the viewport are not realized. Their extent is estimated from the average of the last hundred measured lines, so the scroll extent can shift slightly as more of the collection is seen. Use [TileLayoutEngine](#class-tilelayoutengine) when every item is the same size.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> tags = {"news", "sport", "travel", "food", "music"};

auto flow = std::make_unique<ui::WrapLayoutEngine>();
flow->set_min_item_spacing(8.0f);
flow->set_line_spacing(8.0f);
flow->set_line_alignment(ui::ItemsJustification::SpaceBetween);
ui::WrapLayoutEngine* layout = flow.get(); // observer; the repeater owns it

window.set_content(ui::Scroll{
    .height  = 320.0f,
    .content = ui::ForEach<std::string>{
        .items      = tags,
        .layout     = std::move(flow),
        .virtualize = true,
        .item       = [](const std::string& tag) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Button{.text = tag}; },
    },
});

// Later: switch to columns that scroll horizontally.
layout->set_orientation(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
```

## class LinedFlowLayoutEngine

Derives from `ui::VirtualizingLayout`.

A virtualizing layout that puts items of any width on lines of one fixed height, like a photo wall.

Each item keeps its own aspect ratio. Items are measured at the line height and fill each line greedily. One scale factor per line shrinks its items to fit, and with LinedFlowLayoutItemsStretch::Fill it also widens them to reach the edge. Only the lines in the realization rect are realized. The widths of items never measured are estimated from the average aspect ratio. Host it in a [ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach) inside a [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll), or in a [LayoutPanel](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::vector<ui::ImageSource>> photos; // filled as the pictures load

auto layout = std::make_unique<ui::LinedFlowLayoutEngine>();
layout->set_line_height(160.0f);
layout->set_line_spacing(4.0f);
layout->set_min_item_spacing(4.0f);
layout->set_items_stretch(ui::LinedFlowLayoutItemsStretch::Fill);

window.set_content(ui::Scroll{
    .height  = 480.0f,
    .content = ui::ForEach<ui::ImageSource>{
        .items      = photos,
        .layout     = std::move(layout),
        .virtualize = true,
        .item       = [](const ui::ImageSource& photo) -> ui::Spec {
            return ui::Image{.source = photo};
        },
    },
});
```

## class LayoutOwner

What a layout's host does when the layout asks to be redone.

[LayoutPanelControl](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanelcontrol) and [ForEachControl](for-each.md#uiforeachcontrol), the two hosts a [Layout](#uilayout) attaches to, implement it by measuring or arranging themselves again. A layout reaches it through [Layout::invalidate_measure()](#invalidate_measure) and [Layout::invalidate_arrange()](#invalidate_arrange).

Example: 
```cpp
// A custom layout: a property change redoes the host only while one is attached.
class GapLayout : public ui::NonVirtualizingLayout
{
public:
    void set_gap(float gap)
    {
        gap_ = gap;
        if (owner() != nullptr)
        {
            invalidate_measure(); // the host's layout_invalidated(true)
        }
    }

private:
    float gap_ = 0.0f;
};
```

```cpp
LayoutOwner() = default
```


```cpp
LayoutOwner& operator=(const LayoutOwner&) = delete
```

```cpp
virtual void layout_invalidated(bool measure) = 0
```

The layout's properties changed. Measure and arrange again when `measure` is true, else only arrange.

```cpp

```

## struct ItemsChange

A change to a virtualizing layout's collection, as the host hands it to [VirtualizingLayout::on_items_changed()](#on_items_changed).

Hosts build it from their notify_*() calls, such as [ForEachControl::notify_inserted()](for-each.md#notify_inserted). A layout that caches per-item state uses it to shift or drop that state.

Example: 
```cpp
// A layout that caches each item's height.
class CachedRowLayout : public ui::VirtualizingLayout
{
public:
    void on_items_changed(ui::VirtualizingLayoutContext&, const ui::ItemsChange& change) override
    {
        if (change.action == ui::ItemsChangeAction::Add)
        {
            const auto at = heights_.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(change.new_index);
            heights_.insert(at, change.new_count, 0.0f);
        }
        else
        {
            heights_.clear();
        }
        invalidate_measure();
    }

private:
    std::vector<float> heights_;
};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ItemsChangeAction` | `ItemsChangeAction::Reset` | The kind of change. The [ItemsChangeAction](#itemschangeaction) says which index and count fields apply. |
| `old_index` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The first affected item before the change (Remove, Replace, Move). |
| `old_count` | `std::size_t` | `0` | How many items were removed, replaced or moved. |
| `new_index` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The first affected item after the change (Add, Replace, Move). |
| `new_count` | `std::size_t` | `0` | How many items were inserted or replaced in. |

## class NonVirtualizingLayoutContext

The children of a panel, as a non-virtualizing layout sees them.

The host implements it. A layout calls it only from its [measure()](#measure) and [arrange()](#arrange). Children are addressed by index, in the host's child order, and all of them exist up front.

Example: 
```cpp
class ColumnLayout : public ui::NonVirtualizingLayout
{
public:
    ui::Size measure(ui::NonVirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size available) override
    {
        ui::Size total{};
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < context.item_count(); ++i)
        {
            const ui::Size d = context.measure(i, {available.width, ui::Unbounded});
            total.width = std::max(total.width, d.width);
            total.height += d.height;
        }
        return total;
    }
};
```



Places child `index`, in coordinates relative to the host's content box.

## class VirtualizingLayoutContext

A collection, as a virtualizing layout sees it.

The host implements it: [ForEachControl](for-each.md#uiforeachcontrol), or [LayoutPanelControl](../layout/layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanelcontrol), where every child counts as realized. A layout calls it only from its [measure()](#measure) and [arrange()](#arrange). It asks only for the items that fall in [realization_rect()](#realization_rect), measures and arranges them through the context, and lets the host recycle the rest.

Example: 
```cpp
// Realizes and measures the rows, 32 high, that fall in the realization rect.
void measure_rows(ui::VirtualizingLayoutContext& context, ui::Size available)
{
    const ui::Rect view  = context.realization_rect();
    const auto     first = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(0.0f, view.y) / 32.0f);
    for (std::size_t i = first; i < context.item_count() && static_cast<float>(i) * 32.0f < view.bottom(); ++i)
    {
        ui::Element& e = context.get_or_create_element_at(i);
        (void)context.measure(e, {available.width, ui::Unbounded});
    }
}
```

### ~VirtualizingLayoutContext

```cpp
virtual ~VirtualizingLayoutContext() = default
```

## Enumerations

### ItemsJustification

```cpp
enum class ItemsJustification
```

Where the items of a line go in the room left over along it (a [LinedFlowLayout](#uilinedflowlayout)'s or [TileLayout](#uitilelayout)'s [ItemsJustification](#itemsjustification), a [WrapLayout](#uiwraplayout)'s line alignment).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Start` | Packed at the start (the default). |
| `Center` | Packed in the middle. |
| `End` | Packed at the end. |
| `SpaceAround` | Equal room around each item, so half as much at the ends. |
| `SpaceBetween` | First and last item at the ends, equal gaps between the rest. |
| `SpaceEvenly` | Equal gaps between the items and at both ends. |

### ItemsChangeAction

```cpp
enum class ItemsChangeAction
```

What kind of change it was.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Add` | `new_count` items inserted at `new_index` |
| `Remove` | `old_count` items removed from `old_index` |
| `Replace` | `old_count` items at `old_index` replaced by `new_count` new ones |
| `Move` | `old_count` items moved from `old_index` to `new_index` |
| `Reset` | anything else: the whole collection is new |

### ElementRealizationOptions

```cpp
enum class ElementRealizationOptions : unsigned
```

How get_or_create_element_at() hands an element out. Combine with `|`, test with [has_flag()](#has_flag).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Realize it normally; the host recycles it after a pass that did not ask for it. |
| `ForceCreate` | Realize it even outside the collection's realized range, where the host would otherwise refuse. Use it to measure a representative item. |
| `SuppressAutoRecycle` | The layout keeps track of it and recycles it itself. The host does not clear it at the end of a pass that did not ask for it. |

### LinedFlowLayoutItemsStretch

```cpp
enum class LinedFlowLayoutItemsStretch
```

Whether lines narrower than the room are widened to fill it.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | lines keep their natural width and are placed by [ItemsJustification](#itemsjustification) (the default) |
| `Fill` | every line but the last is scaled up to run edge to edge |

### TileLayoutItemsStretch

```cpp
enum class TileLayoutItemsStretch
```

Whether cells grow to use the leftover room on a line.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Cells keep their size (the default). |
| `Fill` | Cells widen (along the line) so the line fills the available size. |
| `Uniform` | As [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill), and the other dimension grows in proportion. |
